desc:
Houses stand along a road in the order given by positions (coordinates, not necessarily sorted). The road crew cuts the list into two non-empty groups: a prefix (the first k houses) and the remaining suffix, with 1 ≤ k < n. Each group picks its own meeting point (any integer coordinate), and every house walks |x - meeting point| to the point of its group.

Return the smallest possible total walking distance over all choices of k and both meeting points.

positions = [1, 2, 9, 10, 3]
k=2: [1,2] costs 1, [9,10,3] costs 7 (meet at 9)  -> 8
k=4: [1,2,9,10] costs 8, [3] costs 0               -> 8
k=1: 0 + 14 = 14,   k=3: 8 + 7 = 15
answer = 8
hints: For a fixed split the two groups are independent, and each group's best meeting point is a median. So you need the gathering cost of every prefix and of every suffix.
Prefix costs: insert houses one by one into a two-heap median structure that also keeps the sum of each half. Suffix costs: do the same on the reversed array.
Then answer = the minimum over k of prefixCost[k] + suffixCost[k].
editorial: Fix the cut position. The total distance is the cost of the prefix plus the cost of the suffix, and each part is minimised independently by meeting at its median. So the problem reduces to computing cost(positions[0..k)) for all k and cost(positions[k..n)) for all k, then taking the best sum.

Prefix costs come from the standard two-heap routine: a max-heap for the lower half, a min-heap for the upper half, and sums of both halves; the cost after each insertion is sum(hi) - sum(lo) + (|lo| - |hi|) * median. Running the same routine on the reversed array yields the suffix costs.

Two passes of O(n log n) plus an O(n) scan give O(n log n) time and O(n) space. Trying every split with a fresh sort would be O(n<sup>2</sup> log n). The two parts never share a meeting point, so no interaction needs to be modelled.
solution:
import heapq


def _prefix_costs(a):
    lo, hi = [], []
    slo = shi = 0
    out = []
    for x in a:
        if not lo or x <= -lo[0]:
            heapq.heappush(lo, -x)
            slo += x
        else:
            heapq.heappush(hi, x)
            shi += x
        if len(lo) > len(hi) + 1:
            y = -heapq.heappop(lo)
            heapq.heappush(hi, y)
            slo -= y
            shi += y
        elif len(hi) > len(lo):
            y = heapq.heappop(hi)
            heapq.heappush(lo, -y)
            shi -= y
            slo += y
        out.append(shi - slo + (len(lo) - len(hi)) * -lo[0])
    return out


def bestSplitCost(positions):
    n = len(positions)
    pre = _prefix_costs(positions)             # pre[i] = cost of positions[0..i]
    suf = _prefix_costs(positions[::-1])       # suf[j] = cost of the last j + 1 houses
    best = None
    for k in range(1, n):                      # prefix = first k houses, suffix = last n - k houses
        total = pre[k - 1] + suf[n - k - 1]
        if best is None or total < best:
            best = total
    return best
